title: A common divisor divides the gcd
statement: For all natural numbers a, b and c: if a divides b and a divides c, then a divides gcd(b, c).

formal.statement: theorem Nat.dvd_gcd : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat.dvd x0 x1) -> ((x4 : AxNat.dvd x0 x2) -> AxNat.dvd x0 (AxNat.gcd x1 x2))))))

evidence.supports: For all natural numbers a, b and c: if a divides b and a divides c, then a divides gcd(b, c).
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- dvd_gcd 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.dvd_gcd[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so producing this row at all is a machine-checked proof. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and the `grep -q` requires the admitted declaration to be printed -- both halves of the check depend on the theorem actually being present.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `nat_axiom_inventory --require-axiom-free nat` enumerates the built Nat environment and exits non-zero unless it admits no Axiom, Opaque or Quotient declaration (measured: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0). A theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain, so an empty trusted surface bounds every individual theorem's footprint by [].

provenance.source: one of the theorems build_nat_prelude admits; registered to close the flywheel's fact-ledger arrow for recently landed Nat theorems

notes: `depends_on` is literal, not thematic: `theorem_dependency_inventory` reports `Nat.dvd_gcd`'s direct theorem dependencies as `Nat.dvd_mod_iff, Nat.gcd_succ, Nat.gcd_zero_left, Nat.le_succ_succ, Nat.mod_lt, Nat.zero_le` -- of those, only `Nat.gcd_succ` and `Nat.mod_lt` currently have a fact ledger entry, so those two are listed here rather than the full proof-term closure.
